title: Repairing covariance functions on metric trees through a Hausdorff-type distance
summary: A compact metric tree is the natural domain of spatial data recorded along a river network, a root system, or the branched processes of a cell, and a suitable distance between two points is the length of the path joining them. That distance admits almost none of the covariance models of spatial statistics, since only the roughest members of each family stay nonnegative definite, and the resulting fields are nowhere mean square differentiable.
